To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of MD, SMD and SCWRL procedures is a good way to build a realistic coiled-coil structure, that the 5.14 A meridian zone is the most sensitive to the configuration of the side chains, and that a good agreement between the experimental and simulated diffraction patterns is a reliable indicator that the side chains have been correctly positioned.
the side chains in coiled coil protein structures may be positioned by combining molecular dynamics simulations with rotameric side-chain representation and x-ray fiber diffractions.

a coiled coil heterodimeric structure can be built using MD simulations and rotameric side chain positioning, followed by energy minimization, and finally by side chain optimization using the SMD procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of x-ray diffraction and modeling techniques to build a realistic coiled-coil structure.
the development of a method to build a realistic structure for a coiled coil heterodimer using a combined approach of experimental data and simulation techniques.
the use of experimental and computational techniques for refining a cooled coil structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chi(1)(1) dihederal angle distribution along the coiled coil sequence, as well as the chi(1,2) and chi(2,3) dihederals, is the result of a combination of the side chain and the backbone conformational equilibrium.
a realistic coiled coiled structure can be obtained by using the MD procedure followed by the side chain positioning using either SMD or SCRWL.
the best procedure for building a realistic structure is based on the MD equilibration of the side chains and backbone and on the side chain positioning using the SCWRL procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a coiled coil heterodimeric structure can be built by using the MD procedure to equilibrate the side chains, followed by the SCWRL procedure to refine the backbone, and the MD procedure to optimize the side chains.

the chi(1)(-1) dihelicoid angle is a key parameter for the coiled coil structure and that its value along the coiled coil sequence can be estimated using a combined experimental and simulation approach.
the chi(1)/chi(2) dihedral angles are not uniformly distributed, as assumed in previous works.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the coiled coil protein, the chi(1)/chi(2) side chain dihedral angles can be determined using x-ray diffraction and molecular simulations.
a coiled coil can be built by using the experimental diffraction pattern and the chi(1)-angle distribution obtained by MD simulations.
the 5. 15 A meridian diffraction pattern is very sensitive to the side chain positioning and that it can be used for refining coiled coil structures.
